title: Sweet Corn and Goat Cheese Cream
description: Pureed sweet corn balances tangy fresh goat cheese in a cream sauce for salmon, chicken or soft polenta.
equipment: Immersion blender and tall heatproof jug

steps.title: Simmer the corn
steps.text: Combine {corn}, {broth} and {nutmeg} in the HexClad. Cover and simmer for 6–8 minutes until a kernel crushes easily.

steps.title: Blend the corn cream
steps.text: Puree the hot corn mixture with {milk}. Press through a fine sieve into the skillet to catch the kernel skins.

steps.title: Stir the slurry
steps.text: Stir {starch} into {water} in a small cup until smooth.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the sauce to a simmer. Stir in the freshly mixed slurry and cook for about 1 minute, whisking until it coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Set the reduction
steps.text: Measure the base and return it to the skillet. Aim for about 1 3/8 cups. If needed, simmer briefly to reduce or add a splash of water to reach the mark.

steps.title: Melt the goat cheese
steps.text: Take the skillet off heat and gradually whisk in {cheese} until the sauce is smooth and glossy.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Spoon under salmon or around sliced chicken. Ladle more over each portion as desired.

notes: Yield: 1 1/2 cups. One serving is 1/4 cup. Make ahead: The strained corn base can be refrigerated a day ahead. Warm it before adding the slurry and goat cheese. Refrigerate in shallow covered portions within 2 hours and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. For the smoothest finish, freeze the corn base for up to 2 months and add the goat cheese after reheating. Whisk any already-finished thawed portion thoroughly. Fridge reheat: Reheat a portion over medium-low heat, whisking to a brief boil and at least 165°F. Whisk off heat until smooth. Freezer reheat: Thaw in the refrigerator overnight and reheat as for a chilled portion. Option A uses fresh goat cheese. For gentler Option B, use mild part-skim ricotta and briefly blend the finished sauce. For dairy-free sauce, use plain unsweetened oat milk and whipped dairy-free cream cheese. Estimated nutrition per serving (1/6 of recipe): 40 kcal, 2.5 g protein, 5.3 g total carbohydrate, 1.2 g fat, 0.3 g fiber, 39 mg sodium. The estimate covers the prepared condiment. Add separately served foods when totaling a meal. Fiber is estimated before straining.
